findings.passage: I support Governor Tony Evers' leadership to prevent gun violence in our communities. The new Wisconsin Office of Violence Prevention will improve safety and help Wisconsin residents feel secure in their communities. Our constituents want their leaders to take action now.
findings.note: Statement in his own media release backing the governor's executive order creating the Office of Violence Prevention. The printed date reads January 14, 2024, but the file was created 2025-01-14 and he took office in January 2025, so month precision is used. The statement is about gun violence prevention in general and names no specific firearm law.

findings.motion: Introduction of AJR 61 as one of the introducing sponsors (co-sponsorship; not the lead sponsor)
findings.note: AJR 61 proclaims June 6, 2025 as Gun Violence Awareness Day in Wisconsin. He is named among the 30 representatives who introduced it. It was referred to the Committee on Rules. A ceremonial resolution that sets no firearm rule.

findings.passage: Parents should be able to send their children to school for eight hours a day knowing they'll have mental health support and be safe from gun violence.
findings.note: From the 'Meet Andrew' page on his official site, describing what he believes. The page carries no date. It names safety from gun violence at school but no specific gun law. [kept from the first search pass]
